title: Rare tenses and literary periphrases
summary: Recognise the tenses and verb phrases of literary and press Spanish: hubo terminado, la que fuera ministra, habría confesado, habrá llegado, and periphrases such as romper a llorar or llevo leídas cien páginas.
focus: The pretérito anterior, -ra as a pluperfect, the conditional of rumour, the future perfect of conjecture and literary periphrases
content:
## The pretérito anterior: hubo terminado

The **pretérito anterior** is **hube, hubiste, hubo, hubimos, hubisteis, hubieron** + participle. It marks an action completed *immediately* before another past action, and it appears almost only after time conjunctions: **apenas, en cuanto, tan pronto como, una vez que, no bien, luego que**.

- **Apenas hubo terminado el discurso, abandonó la sala.** (No sooner had he finished the speech than he left the room.)
- **Una vez que hubo salido el tren, la estación quedó en silencio.** (Once the train had left, the station fell silent.)

Today it is literary or deliberately solemn. Speech and most writing use the preterite (**apenas terminó**), the pluperfect (**cuando había terminado**) or a participle clause (**terminado el discurso**).

## -ra as a pluperfect: el que fuera ministro

The **-ra** form began life as a pluperfect indicative (Latin *amaveram* gave **amara**), and the press and literary prose keep that use, mostly in relative clauses: **fuera** = **había sido**.

- **Elena Prado, la que fuera alcaldesa de la ciudad, publica sus memorias.** (Elena Prado, the former mayor of the city, is publishing her memoirs.)
- **El edificio que albergara la vieja fábrica es hoy un museo.** (The building that had housed the old factory is now a museum.)

It sounds elevated, so style guides ask for restraint. **había sido** or **la exalcaldesa** is always correct. Do not confuse it with the subjunctive **-ra** of **si fuera alcaldesa…** (if she were mayor…).

## Rumour and conjecture: habría confesado, habrá llegado

News Spanish often uses the conditional for unconfirmed reports, the **condicional de rumor**:

- **Según fuentes policiales, el detenido habría confesado el robo.** (According to police sources, the detainee has reportedly confessed to the robbery.)

The RAE's *Diccionario panhispánico de dudas* advises against it, and many newsroom style books ban it. People often call it a Gallicism, and it hides who vouches for the fact. Attribute instead: **según la policía, el detenido ha confesado**.

The **future perfect** makes a guess, from the present, about something already done:

- **No contesta; habrá llegado ya al teatro.** (He isn't answering; he must have reached the theatre by now.)
- **¿Quién habrá dejado esto aquí?** (Who can have left this here?)

## Periphrases of onset and approximation

| Periphrasis | Shade | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **venir a** + inf. | roughly, amounts to | **La obra viene a costar un millón.** (The work comes to about a million.) |
| **dar en** + inf. | to take to (an odd or stubborn habit) | **Dio en pensar que el reloj lo vigilaba.** (He took to thinking the clock was watching him.) |
| **romper a** + inf. | to burst out | **El bebé rompió a llorar.** / **Rompió a llover.** |
| **echarse a** + inf. | to start suddenly | **Se echó a reír.** (She burst out laughing.) |
| **no alcanzar a** + inf. | not to manage to, can't quite | **No alcanzo a entender su decisión.** (I can't quite understand her decision.) |

**Romper a** and **echarse a** take only a few verbs: llorar, reír, correr, andar, temblar, and **romper a llover**.

## Periphrases of progress and result

- **ir + gerundio**: gradual progress, step by step. **La plaza se iba llenando de gente.** (The square was gradually filling with people.)
- **llevar + participio**: the amount done so far. **Llevo corregidas cuarenta páginas.** (I've corrected forty pages so far.)
- **tener + participio**: a result in hand, or insistence. **Tengo escritas tres cartas.** (I've got three letters written.) **Te tengo dicho que no toques eso.** (I've told you time and again not to touch that.) Also **tengo entendido que…** (I understand that…, from hearsay).

Unlike **haber**, these participles agree with the object: **he escrito tres cartas**, but **tengo escritas tres cartas**.

vocabulary.meaning: no sooner, as soon as (before a past action); also: hardly
vocabulary.example: Apenas hubo cerrado la carta, llamaron a la puerta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: No sooner had she sealed the letter than someone knocked at the door.

vocabulary.example: Una vez que hubimos firmado, el notario guardó los papeles.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Once we had signed, the notary put the papers away.

vocabulary.meaning: had gone out, had left (pretérito anterior, literary)
vocabulary.example: Cuando el último actor hubo salido, cayó el telón.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When the last actor had gone off, the curtain fell.

vocabulary.term: el que fuera / la que fuera
vocabulary.meaning: the former…, who had been (-ra as a pluperfect)
vocabulary.example: Visitamos la casa del que fuera director del museo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We visited the house of the former director of the museum.

vocabulary.example: Según un diario, el acusado habría confesado ante el juez.
vocabulary.example_meaning: According to one newspaper, the accused has reportedly confessed before the judge.

vocabulary.meaning: has probably arrived, must have arrived (future perfect of conjecture)
vocabulary.example: Son las diez: el paquete habrá llegado a la oficina.
vocabulary.example_meaning: It's ten o'clock: the parcel must have reached the office.

vocabulary.meaning: to come to, to amount roughly to
vocabulary.example: Su respuesta viene a ser un no.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Her answer amounts to a no.

vocabulary.meaning: to take to (doing something odd or stubborn)
vocabulary.example: Mi vecino ha dado en tocar la trompeta a medianoche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My neighbour has taken to playing the trumpet at midnight.

vocabulary.example: Al salir del cine rompió a llover.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As we came out of the cinema it began to pour.

vocabulary.example: Los niños se echaron a correr hacia la playa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The children broke into a run towards the beach.

vocabulary.meaning: not to manage to, can't quite
vocabulary.example: No alcanzo a ver la diferencia entre las dos versiones.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I can't quite see the difference between the two versions.

vocabulary.example: Con los años fue aprendiendo a callar.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Over the years he gradually learnt to hold his tongue.

vocabulary.meaning: to have (so far) done; the participle agrees
vocabulary.example_meaning: We've sold two hundred tickets so far.

vocabulary.example: Te tengo dicho que no dejes la puerta abierta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I've told you over and over not to leave the door open.

quiz.prompt: Apenas ___ terminado la sesión, el juez se levantó.
quiz.explanation: Apenas takes the pretérito anterior (hubo + participle), an action completed just before another past action (se levantó).
hints: The main verb is a preterite; you need the past of haber that pairs with it.

quiz.prompt: Una vez que los invitados ___ salido, cerraron las puertas. (pretérito anterior of haber)
quiz.explanation: Third person plural of the pretérito anterior: hubieron salido. Everyday Spanish would say habían salido or simply salieron.

quiz.prompt: Which is the everyday way to say: Apenas hubo llegado, pidió un café?
options: Apenas ha llegado, pidió un café.
quiz.explanation: The simple preterite has replaced the pretérito anterior in speech and most prose: apenas llegó.
hints: The modern replacement keeps the narrative in the preterite.

quiz.prompt: Ana Ruiz, la que fuera ministra de Cultura, presenta hoy su libro. Here fuera means…
options: had been (she is the former minister)
will be (she is about to become minister)
quiz.correct_answer: had been (she is the former minister)
quiz.explanation: In journalistic and literary prose, -ra in a relative clause can be a pluperfect indicative: la que fuera ministra = la que había sido ministra.
hints: There is no condition and no wish here. It is a fact about her past.
teaches: el que fuera / la que fuera

quiz.prompt: True or false: the RAE's Diccionario panhispánico de dudas recommends the conditional of rumour (El detenido habría confesado) for news writing.
quiz.explanation: It advises against it, as do many newsroom style books. State the source instead (según la policía, el detenido ha confesado).
hints: Think about who vouches for an unconfirmed report.

quiz.prompt: No contesta al teléfono; ya ___ salido de casa. (a guess: he has probably left)
quiz.explanation: The future perfect expresses a conjecture about something already done: habrá salido = he has probably left.

quiz.prompt: El informe viene a decir que no hay dinero. Viene a decir means…
options: more or less says, amounts to saying
is coming in order to say
quiz.correct_answer: more or less says, amounts to saying
quiz.explanation: Venir a + infinitive marks approximation: the report's message comes down to that.
hints: It does not describe movement, and it does not mean acabar de.

quiz.prompt: Al leer la carta, la abuela rompió ___ llorar.
quiz.explanation: Romper a + infinitive marks a sudden, unstoppable start (rompió a llorar = she burst into tears).
hints: The same preposition as in echarse ___ reír.

quiz.prompt: En su vejez, el pintor dio en creer que sus cuadros hablaban. Dio en creer means…
quiz.explanation: Dar en + infinitive means to take to doing something, usually odd or obstinate.
hints: It describes a new habit of mind, often a strange one.

quiz.prompt: Llevo ___ ochenta páginas de la novela. (leer, agreeing with páginas)
quiz.explanation: With llevar + participle, the participle agrees with the object: llevo leídas ochenta páginas.

listening.note: Romper a + infinitive: a sudden start.

listening.meaning: She must have got home by now.
listening.note: Future perfect: a guess about something already done.

listening.text: Los actores se echaron a reír en el ensayo.
listening.meaning: The actors burst out laughing at the rehearsal.
listening.note: New word: el ensayo = the rehearsal.

listening.text: No alcanzo a leer la letra del médico.
listening.meaning: I can't quite read the doctor's handwriting.
listening.note: New word: la letra = the handwriting.

listening.text: Llevo escritas veinte cartas desde el lunes.
listening.meaning: I've written twenty letters since Monday.

listening.text: El pueblo se iba vaciando con cada invierno que pasaba.
listening.meaning: The village was slowly emptying with every winter that went by.

listening.text: La que fuera directora del colegio vive ahora en el campo.
listening.meaning: The former head of the school now lives in the countryside.
listening.note: -ra as a pluperfect: fuera = había sido.

listening.text: Apenas hubo cerrado la tienda, el dueño se marchó sin despedirse de nadie.
listening.meaning: No sooner had he closed the shop than the owner left without saying goodbye to anyone.
listening.note: New word: despedirse = to say goodbye.

guide.tip: Ask who vouches for the fact. If it is a source, name it. If it is you guessing, use habrá + participle.

conversations.title: Editing the crime report
conversations.scenario: Lucía, the night editor of a daily paper, goes through Andrés's crime report with him before it goes to print.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Andrés, he leído tu crónica. Tenemos que hablar del titular.
lines.meaning: Andrés, I've read your report. We need to talk about the headline.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Qué le pasa? Decir que el detenido habría confesado me parece prudente.
lines.meaning: What's wrong with it? Saying the detainee has reportedly confessed seems prudent to me.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Prudente no, ambiguo. Si la fuente es la policía, dilo: según la policía, ha confesado.
lines.meaning: Not prudent, vague. If the source is the police, say so: according to the police, he has confessed.
lines.note: Style guides discourage the conditional of rumour.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: De acuerdo. ¿Y lo de la que fuera ministra de Hacienda? ¿También lo cambio?
lines.meaning: All right. And the bit about the former finance minister? Do I change that too?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Eso puede quedarse, aunque exministra viene a decir lo mismo con menos solemnidad.
lines.meaning: That can stay, although former minister says roughly the same with less pomp.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Lo dejo, entonces. ¿Y el segundo párrafo?
lines.meaning: I'll leave it, then. And the second paragraph?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: El de apenas hubo terminado la declaración suena a novela decimonónica.
lines.meaning: The one with no sooner had the statement ended sounds like a nineteenth-century novel.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Tienes razón. Pondré que el juez se retiró en cuanto terminó la declaración.
lines.meaning: You're right. I'll put that the judge withdrew as soon as the statement ended.
lines.note: The modern replacement: en cuanto + preterite.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Mucho mejor. ¿Cuántas piezas llevas escritas hoy?
lines.meaning: Much better. How many pieces have you written so far today?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Llevo escritas tres, y la cuarta se va alargando sin remedio.
lines.meaning: I've written three, and the fourth keeps getting longer and longer.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: El director habrá leído ya el borrador. Mándame la versión final antes de las ocho.
lines.meaning: The editor-in-chief will have read the draft by now. Send me the final version before eight.

bites.title: Hubo terminado
bites.rule: Pretérito anterior = hube, hubo… + participle, right after apenas, en cuanto, una vez que. Literary today: say apenas terminó or cuando había terminado.
bites.example_meaning: No sooner had he finished than he left.

bites.title: Fuera = había sido
bites.rule: In the press, -ra can be a pluperfect: la que fuera ministra means the former minister. Había sido or exministra is always safe.
bites.example: El que fuera alcalde abre una librería.
bites.example_meaning: The former mayor is opening a bookshop.

bites.title: Rumour and guesswork
bites.rule: Habría confesado means reportedly confessed. The RAE's DPD discourages it, so name the source. Habrá llegado means has probably arrived, and it is your own guess.
bites.example_meaning: She isn't answering: she must have left already.

bites.title: Periphrases with a shade
bites.rule: venir a = roughly; dar en = take to; romper a / echarse a = burst out; no alcanzar a = can't quite; ir + gerund = gradually; llevar / tener + agreeing participle.
bites.example_meaning: I've corrected ten pages so far.

sorts.title: Which rare tense?

items.text: el edificio que albergara la fábrica

sorts.why: Hubo + participle follows apenas; -ra in a relative clause looks back; habría reports a rumour; habrá guesses from now.

sorts.title: Which shade?
sorts.why: Romper a and echarse a start suddenly; ir + gerund and llevar / tener + participle build up; venir a approximates and no alcanzar a falls short.

spots.sentence: Apenas ha terminado el discurso, abandonó la sala.
spots.why: In a past narrative after apenas: hubo terminado (literary) or simply terminó.
With llevar + participle, the participle agrees with the object: páginas.

spots.sentence: Al oír el chiste, se echó en reír.
spots.why: Echarse a + infinitive: se echó a reír.

spots.sentence: No contesta; habría llegado ya al teatro.
spots.why: A guess about now uses the future perfect: habrá llegado.

spots.sentence: Mi tío dio a pensar que los vecinos lo espiaban.
spots.why: Dar en + infinitive = to take to doing something odd.

builds.text: Apenas hubo salido, empezó a llover.
builds.meaning: No sooner had she gone out than it started to rain.

builds.text: La que fuera ministra publica sus memorias.
builds.meaning: The former minister is publishing her memoirs.

builds.text: Se echó a reír sin motivo.
builds.meaning: He burst out laughing for no reason.

builds.text: La sala se iba llenando poco a poco.
builds.meaning: The hall was filling up little by little.
